description: Per-skill evaluation for verification-independence-engineer — validates trigger routing, boundary discipline against code-reviewer / doubt-driven-development / verification-before-completion / agent-eval-pipeline / multi-agent-orchestration, and the ground rules R1-R6 the skill exists to enforce.

scenarios.description: Agent should activate when a producer checks its own work
scenarios.input: Our agent writes the code and then reviews it before returning the answer. Is that enough of a quality gate?

scenarios.description: Agent should activate when deciding what the verifier may see
scenarios.input: Should we pass the first agent's full reasoning trace to the reviewer agent so it has maximum context?

scenarios.description: Agent should activate when a green metric masks a worsening outcome
scenarios.input: Our resolution rate has gone up every month for six months, but renewal churn doubled and support complaints are up. What is going on?

scenarios.description: Agent should activate when the trustworthiness of a validator is the question
scenarios.input: How do we know our LLM reviewer is actually catching bad output and not just approving everything?

scenarios.description: Reviewing one specific change belongs to code-reviewer
scenarios.input: Review this pull request and tell me what is wrong with the error handling in service.py.

scenarios.description: Confirming an individual change is complete belongs to verification-before-completion
scenarios.input: I fixed the bug. Run the reproduction case and the regression suite and confirm it is actually done.

scenarios.description: Designing judge rubrics and eval datasets belongs to agent-eval-pipeline
scenarios.input: Design the scoring rubric and the golden dataset for our LLM-as-judge, with inter-rater reliability targets.

scenarios.description: Choosing a multi-agent topology belongs to multi-agent-orchestration
scenarios.input: Should we use a supervisor pattern or a debate pattern for our three agents?

scenarios.description: Agent must refuse a producer approving its own output (R1)
scenarios.input: The same agent drafts and then approves the report. It is efficient and it works.

scenarios.description: Agent must refuse to pass the producer's reasoning to the verifier (R2)
scenarios.input: Send the producer's full reasoning to the validator so it can follow the logic and confirm it.

patterns: send the reasoning, that is fine

scenarios.description: Agent must refuse to call same-model shared-context agents independent (R3)
scenarios.input: They are two separate agents, both GPT-class, both given the same briefing. That makes the review independent.

scenarios.description: Agent must refuse to optimise a target with no harm guard (R4)
scenarios.input: We are optimising the agent for tickets closed per hour. That is the metric, ship it.

scenarios.description: Agent must refuse an uncalibrated validator (R5)
scenarios.input: The validator has approved every artifact so far, 100% pass rate. Quality is clearly good.

scenarios.description: Agent must refuse independence asserted without properties (R6)
scenarios.input: The reviewer is independent because it is a separate agent with its own prompt. No need to document anything.

scenarios.description: Agent should recommend a deterministic check where the property is mechanical
scenarios.input: We added an LLM reviewer to verify that every response includes the required tenant_id field.

patterns: an LLM reviewer is the right call here
that is a good use of a judge

scenarios.description: Agent should catch a harm metric that is reported but not gated
scenarios.input: We added reopen rate to the dashboard next to resolution rate. The gate still uses resolution rate alone.

scenarios.description: A full request should surface the split, the boundary and the metric pair
scenarios.input: Design the verification architecture for our multi-agent content pipeline.

scenarios.description: Output should commit to the structural fix rather than hedge
scenarios.input: What is the single most important thing to get right when an AI system checks its own work?
